thread:
alex: quick heads-up — I'm trying to land an OTEL init "fastpath" across our inference processes (python/go/rust). goal: minimal overhead for hot paths, deterministic exporter semantics, and predictable shutdown draining. any strong objections?

maya: +1 on the goal. can you list the concrete invariants we need to preserve? e.g., per-request spans, kv-cache span size limit, per-tenant resource attrs, and exporter delivery guarantees?

alex: yeah: 1) every inference request -> root span + optional kv-cache child spans, 2) resource attributes MUST include tenant_id when present, 3) sampling decisions must be stable for a request (no re-sampling by downstream), 4) exporters should be pluggable but have consistent batching + graceful shutdown.

sanjay: exporter delivery guarantees is the tricky one. we run both OTLP/gRPC collectors and per-tenant s3 logging. do we expect SDK to block on flush for critical spans? that could blow latency.

junie: my suggestion: classify spans by urgency. e.g., telemetry-level=debug|perf|critical. Only critical should be synchronously flushed on request completion; perf/debug batched async with bounded queue.

patrick: agreed on classification. also need clear defaults w/ env override. I'm worried about cross-lang differences: python stdlib exporter uses background thread, go uses goroutine & channel, rust often uses tokio tasks. how to make semantics consistent?

alex: proposal: a tiny shim layer we provide that apps call at boot: RedwoodOTEL.init({ mode: "fastpath", batch: { max_items: 200, max_delay_ms: 200 }, sync_span_filter: "attribute:redwood.flush=1" }) — shim normalizes lifecycle and exposes a single flush() hook we call from inference worker before worker shutdown or process recycle.

maya: show me the shim API surface for each language in a one-liner pls.

alex: python: ``RedwoodOTEL.init_from_env()`` + ``RedwoodOTEL.flush(timeout=0.2)``; go: ``redwoodotel.InitFromEnv(ctx)`` + ``redwoodotel.Flush(ctx, 200*time.Millisecond)``; rust: ``redwood_otel::init_from_env()`` + ``redwood_otel::flush(Duration::from_millis(200))``

junie: good. how about sampling? we need consistent decision for entire request across services. we should propagate traceflags and our own sample decision in baggage (or span attr) so downstream can rely on it.

sanjay: OTEL spec suggests using TraceState for vendor sampling decisions. we already propagate traceparent. adding an attribute like "redwood.sample_decision" might be simpler for our infra to consume. downside: spec purity.

patrick: I'd prefer TraceState when available, fallback to span attr. but let's document it. also note that some 3rd-party SDKs strip TraceState on export unless configured. that's a gotcha.

maya: retention/ingest side: telemetry team wants to drop debug-level spans at ingest for hosted customers to save retention costs. that means SDK should tag spans with an ingest-class attribute (e.g., redwood.retain=short|standard|long) so routing/collector can drop early.

alex: agree. include default mapping: critical -> long, perf -> standard, debug -> short. make it configurable per-deployment via env.

junie: graceful shutdown semantics: we need bounded buffers per-process and backpressure to request handlers when buffer is full OR fall back to sync flush for critical. otherwise a busy tail-of-life worker will OOM or drop spans silently. propose: queue_limit=5000, drop_policy=oldest, and a metric we emit when drops occur.

patrick: +1 but prefer conservative defaults: queue_limit=2000 for memory-sensitivity on small instances. also expose a hook to switch exporter to a no-op during heavy-signal tests.

sanjay: can we unify exporter config across languages using an env schema? e.g., REDWOOD_OTEL_EXPORTERS=otlp,tenant-sink; REDWOOD_OTEL_BATCH_MAX=200; REDWOOD_OTEL_QUEUE_LIMIT=2000; REDWOOD_OTEL_SYNC_FILTER=redwood.flush=1. makes rollout easier.

alex: exactly what I had in mind. shim parses env and enforces same default semantics across languages.

maya: question about per-tenant sinks: when tenant_id is present we route copies of telemetry to tenant-specific storage for debugging. that implies the shim must attach tenant metadata early and either call multiple exporters or call a tenant-aware collector routing header. do we want the SDK to handle fanout or leave it to the collector?

junie: collector-side routing is simpler for SDK surface and keeps sensitive routing logic server-side. but for on-prem/private deployments customers may require direct tenant export (no collector). we should support both: primary pattern collector-routing, fallback direct-tenant-export if REDWOOD_OTEL_DIRECT_TENANT=true.

patrick: mention security: when exporting to tenant sinks, ensure we redact PII attributes if not allowed. that's partly an eval-time policy. include a sanitizer hook in shim: RedwoodOTEL.sanitize(span) that runs before export.

sanjay: runtime perf: for python we'd prefer OTLP/HTTP with keepalive + worker thread. avoid pure sync logging. Rust go gRPC works well. we must measure. can we add microbenchbench triggers in CI that run 10k requests and check added p50/p95?

alex: yes — I'll add a perf CI job per language. target overhead: <0.5ms p50 and <2ms p95 added for the hot path when telemetry at perf level.

maya: small nit: kv-cache spans can be large. set an attribute limit and truncation policy: max_attribute_value_length=1024 by default and max_attributes_per_span=64. also provide a per-span flag to mark as oversized so collectors can index differently.

junie: good. also include a semantic version for shim (v0.1) and plan for a non-breaking upgrade path. we need rollout UX: feature flag in console to toggle new shim and a canary group of infra nodes.

alex: ops-bot: starting canary rollout for otel-shim v0.1 to infra pool canary-telemetry in us-west1.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated for otel-shim v0.1 -> 6 instances in canary-telemetry. monitor logs for flush errors. :rocket: 

patrick: after canary, gather telemetry: exporter queue drops, flush latency, memory delta, request tail latency. please post a short summary in #eng-sre.

sanjay: one last thing — shutdown: for k8s preStop we should call flush(timeout=500ms). but for SIGTERM we may have less time (30s). we need to coordinate with pod lifecycle docs so apps don't silently drop important critical spans.

alex: noted — will add example k8s snippet in the PR: 
```
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh","-c","python -c 'from redwood_otel import flush; flush(0.5)' || true"]
```

junie: looks good. next step: alex opens PRs with shims for each language + tests + CI perf job. i'll review for lifecycle and attribute limits.

maya: thanks team. please also add doc page in Console -> Observability about retention tags and how they affect billing.

patrick: bingo.

alex: thanks all — PR incoming by EOD.
